world.bio: I'm Daniel, twenty-eight, a machine learning engineer at a mid-size startup in San Francisco. I work on recommendation ranking, which basically means I decide what you see next. I'm good at it and increasingly tired of optimising click-through. I rent a windowless room for $3,600 a month, climb at Mission Cliffs on weekends, and am learning Mandarin so I can talk to my grandmother, who speaks to me in Hokkien and thinks I'm a disgrace. I have started waking at 4 a.m. worrying about the next layoff round and haven't told anyone.
skills_assets: Three years building ranking and recommendation models in PyTorch and LightGBM
A feature store, offline evaluation harness and A/B test pipeline he helped build at his current company
Comfortable with Python, SQL, Spark and some Rust
A collection of Mandarin flashcards on Anki: 1,140 cards and a 62-day streak
Climbing gear and a membership at Mission Cliffs
A personal GitHub with a couple of small open-source tools
A modest equity grant that is currently worth less than the exercise price

projects.name: Ranking model v3
projects.text: I'm leading the third iteration of our feed ranking model. The goal is a 2% lift in click-through. We are already at diminishing returns. My manager wants it by quarter end. What I really want is to optimise for something other than clicks, like the number of people who say 'that was useful' in surveys, but no one has funded that metric.

projects.name: Mandarin for Nai Nai
projects.text: My grandmother, Nai Nai, speaks Hokkien and a little Mandarin. I speak English and my mother's mangled Cantonese. I'm learning Mandarin so I can have an actual conversation with her before she's too old. Practice every morning on the BART, 25 minutes.

projects.name: Climbing project
projects.text: Working a V6 at Mission Cliffs called 'The Quiet One'. Haven't sent it in three weeks.

notes.text: 4:04 a.m. Woke up. Brain went: layoff, layoff, layoff. I counted the number of people on my team (nine) and the number of people on the team that got cut in June (all of them). Lay there until 5:30 and then gave up and made coffee.
Climbed at Mission Cliffs. Fell off the V6 four times. A kid of maybe fourteen sent it first go and then offered me beta. Took it. Sent it on the next attempt. Felt ridiculous and happy.
Sprint review. My model's offline gain was 1.4%. Product asked why not 2%. I said the baseline is already tuned to death. VP said 'find a way'. Everyone nodded. I nodded too.

Rent increase notice from the landlord: $3,750 from December. For a room with no window. Can't afford to move, can't afford to stay. Looked at Oakland rooms. They all had windows. Considered it a sign.

Nai Nai video call. I said 'wo xiang ni' (I miss you). She laughed so hard she coughed. Then she said something in Hokkien I didn't catch and my mum, in the background, translated: 'You sound like a robot.' Best compliment all week.
Read about a competitor laying off 12%. Our CEO wrote 'we're well funded' in Slack. Everyone knows what that means. I opened LinkedIn and closed it again six times.
Anki streak at 58. Cards are getting harder. Learned 'yǒudiǎnr' vs 'yìdiǎnr'. Still can't tell when to use which. Also learned the word for 'recommend': tuījiàn. Of course.
Told my friend Eli I'm 'fine' at work. He asked how many hours I sleep. I said six. Lied. It's about four. If I say it out loud it becomes real.
Quarterly all-hands tomorrow. Everyone on Slack posting memes about 'surviving the offsite'. I am drafting my resume in a text file called 'notes_do_not_open'.

messages.text:
Mum: Did you eat?
Me: Yes, Ma.
Mum: What did you eat?
Me: Pasta.
Mum: That's not food.

Eli: Climb Saturday?
Me: Yes. Send the V6 beta again.
Eli: Why do you keep falling off it?
Me: I'm optimising for failure.

Priyanka: Quick sync tomorrow?
Me: Sure. About what?
Priyanka: Just planning.
Me: Great.

Nai Nai: Tell him he should eat rice.
Mum: She says eat rice.
Me: Tell her I'm learning the word for rice.
Mum: She says that's not the same as eating it.

relations.about: Grandmother in Penang, speaks Hokkien, teases his Mandarin.
Calls often, worries about his diet.

Would rather work on something less about attention
